_comment: Access classification rules template for a new U.S. state. Copy this file to access-rules/<statename>.json (e.g. access-rules/montana.json). State rules receive a +1000 priority boost over national rules in _national.json, so they always win when they match. No code changes required to add a state.
_comment_scope: Lowercase state name, matching the filename without .json (e.g. montana).
description: One sentence describing the rule sources and key data providers for this state.

rules._comment: One rule object per classification decision. Rules are evaluated in descending priority order. The highest-priority matching rule wins. Ties go to Unknown (Category 5) — ambiguity always fails toward safe.
rules._comment_id: Lowercase, underscores. Must be unique across ALL rule files (prefix with state abbreviation, e.g. mt_walk_in).
rules._comment_category: One of: huntable | no_hunting | closed | private | unknown
rules._comment_source_dataset: Displayed in the click-to-inspect popup so users know which dataset drove the classification.
rules.note: Plain-English explanation of WHY this rule assigns this category. Tell the user what to verify. This text appears in the inspection popup.
rules._comment_priority: Integer 1–99 for state rules (they are boosted to 1001–1099 at runtime, beating all national rules). Higher = evaluated first. Use 85–90 for primary access rules, 78–82 for default/fallback state rules, 40–60 for advisory overlays (e.g. checkerboard).

match._comment: ALL conditions in match[] must be true (logical AND).
match._comment_field: GeoJSON attribute field name from the source dataset.
match._comment_op: Comparison operator: eq (equals) | neq (not equals) | contains (substring) | startsWith | endsWith | exists (field is present) | blank (field missing or empty)

match_any._comment: ANY one condition in match_any[] being true satisfies this block (logical OR). Both match[] AND match_any[] must be satisfied when both are non-empty.

rules._comment_example: Example: state walk-in hunting access rule
rules.note: This property is enrolled in the state walk-in hunting access program. Access is seasonal and enrollment changes annually — verify current program maps before hunting.
